# Migration fixture provenance

These SQL files contain synthetic, unreleased M04 schemas and data. They have never been a published Loop database or a user's journal. Product code does not import them. Binary database files remain ignored.

`schema_v1.sql` freezes the initial relational schema before durable file cleanup. `seed_v1.sql` covers every v1 table, including completed manual intent, an exercise snapshot, a versioned reading, a goal and an opaque media reference. Tests create its three synthetic media bytes separately. V2 adds the cleanup queue and cascade trigger without rewriting those values. Schema/version migration commits atomically.

`schema_v2.sql` and its JSON freeze the actual M04 Drift schema. Keep historical v1/v2 unchanged. Current `schema_v3.json` is generated with `dart --suppress-analytics run drift_dev schema dump lib/core/data/database/loop_database.dart test/fixtures/database/schema_v3.json`; its `fixed_sql` SQLite records form `schema_v3.sql`, followed by `PRAGMA user_version = 3`. V3 adds optional goal motivation and retains completion metadata when archiving. Tests compare real migrated/fresh schemas, indexes, triggers, every prior row/column, foreign keys and queued work. An interruption after the actual goals-table rebuild must restore v2 unchanged, then retry successfully. These are upgrade fixtures, never product startup data.

`schema_v4.json` / `schema_v4.sql` add M06 dependent fractional clock/manual-draft checkpoints. Frozen v1–v3 remain unchanged; upgrade tests preserve every historical row and prove rollback after the actual v4 table DDL. These are test-only schemas, never production seed data.

`schema_v5.json` / `schema_v5.sql` add M07 optional What got easier and dependent bounded raw journal drafts. Generated by the pinned Drift schema dump; SQLite fixed SQL plus PRAGMA version5. Frozen v1–v4 remain unchanged. Upgrade tests preserve prior columns/rows and fractional checkpoints, including rollback after actual journal DDL.
